champion.challengeFraming: Name the exact manual process and the role of the person doing it. Use the specific words from their transcript. 'Your {job title} manually {exact process} every {frequency} — that stops on go-live day.' If they said it, use their exact phrasing.
champion.fomoFraming: Lead with hours saved and the specific manual task that disappears. Structure: '{X hours/week} recovered — {the exact task} is gone on go-live day.' No AI framing needed for the hook — Stage 1 outcomes carry the pitch.
champion.journeyFraming: Stage 1 bullet items should read like a 'things that stop happening Monday morning' list. Use active verbs: 'stops,' 'disappears,' 'no longer.' Stage 2 gets two sentences. Stage 3 gets one — plant the seed without over-pitching to someone who wants immediate relief.
champion.closingLineVariant: Stage 1 eliminates the specific manual work your team does today. Stages 2 and 3 build on that foundation — but the immediate win is on go-live day.

economicBuyer.executiveSummaryFraming: Open the executive summary with a Peerless-internal payback anchor — Ashley's ~1.5h/job manual rekey converted to weekly/annual loaded-labor cost, plus Brian Cook's named $5K/month GCP-hosting cost figure — then name the four confirmed flows (UC1–UC4) as the mechanism that recovers that figure. Do NOT lead with the operational pain narrative; lead with the dollar figure. Do NOT reference parent or sibling-company context (Akoya, Imperial Fence, etc.) — keep the executive frame entirely about Peerless. Close with the managed-service line that turns the decision into a single ROI comparison (cost of staying manual vs. monthly service rate).
